State of AI Data Labs and Human Feedback

A selected public-source baseline for buying, building, and evaluating human and model feedback

Prepared 9 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 9 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-09.prelaunch.3

This selected, incomplete prelaunch baseline connects reviewed public disclosures, eight full-source paper works, and scoped dataset and benchmark documentation. It offers sample-limited judgments and practical acceptance questions. It is not a supplier census, a market ranking, a completed launch audit, a human peer-reviewed publication, or an archived edition.

AI-assisted research with Separate AI review. Assertion approval records actual, distinct author, source-verifier, and adversarial source-content invocations; it establishes support for scoped statements, not independent replication or operational certification. Report-level independent review is recorded separately against exact content digests. No human expert review is claimed.

1. Executive assessment

Method

This is a selected baseline, not a comprehensive state-of-market census. The frozen input contains 173 approved assertions, including 163 newly selected assertions and ten carried-forward approvals. Computed qualifying coverage is eight suppliers, eight distinct full-source paper works, eight dataset families and five benchmark families, with eight of 39 legacy organizations dispositioned. Other records remain visible under their actual status; neither assertion volume nor inclusion establishes representative coverage.

Analysis

Within this sample, buying AI data involves several different deliverables: expert-created tasks and rubrics, preference pairs, evaluation datasets, executable environments and participant access. Mercor describes expert-written workplace tasks; Surge markets RL environments and verifiers; Prolific offers participant access and managed collection. These disclosures support requirement-based comparisons. They do not establish interchangeable services, measured capacity or comparative performance.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.mercor.task-construction, candidate.supplier.surge_ai.rl-environments, candidate.supplier.prolific.platform-managed, candidate.supplier.toloka.hybrid-offering

Analysis

Human involvement must be located in the workflow. HelpSteer3-Preference uses independent human preference annotators; UltraFeedback uses GPT-4 labels; FineWeb-Edu develops filtering from Llama-generated educational scores. Calling all three human-feedback data would obscure their different content and label provenance. Buyers should request separate fields for prompt origin, response generation, annotation, filtering and oversight before comparing quantities.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.independent-human-labels, next.claim.ultrafeedback.model_feedback, candidate.paperfull.fineweb.synthetic-educational-labels

Analysis

The reviewed methods also warn against reading a polished dataset as the raw annotation process. HelpSteer3 removes invalid samples and selects agreeing annotations; InstructGPT usually uses one contractor for comparisons; SHP infers collective preferences from existing human-written material. Each creates a different observation unit. A preference-pair count alone cannot determine independent judgments, disagreement coverage or suitability for a particular objective.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.postfilter-consensus, candidate.paperfull.instructgpt.single-contractor-comparisons, next.claim.shp.collective_preferences

Research gap

The launch floors remain unmet: 39 legacy dispositions, 60 qualifying suppliers, 150 reviewed paper works, 60 dataset families, 20 benchmark families and 90% disposition of a frozen eligible core. The core has not been frozen. Neither required real 200-record audit is supplied. No market share, market-wide ranking, research precision, completed human review, DOI or published archive is established by this preparation snapshot.

Analytical judgment

delivery-unit-before-provider

In this reviewed sample, a useful supplier comparison begins with the delivery unit: participant access, licensed data, custom tasks or executable environments.

Buyer implication
Specify who owns task design, annotation, QA, rights clearance and acceptance before comparing proposals.
Limitations
First-party offering descriptions do not establish interchangeable services, capacity, realized quality or a market-wide supplier ranking.
Confidence
Moderate for this sample’s disclosed distinctions; low for prevalence outside it.
Reasoning
Prolific distinguishes participant access and managed collection; Snorkel describes refreshed non-exclusive products; Mercor describes custom task construction; Surge offers environments and verifiers. Their responsibilities differ even where capability labels overlap.
What would change this assessment
Matched statements of work and independently checked deliveries could show that particular offerings meet the same requirement and permit narrower outcome comparisons.

Approved evidence: candidate.supplier.prolific.platform-managed, candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.data-series, candidate.supplier.mercor.task-construction, candidate.supplier.surge_ai.rl-environments

Analytical judgment

human-and-model-provenance

Human content, human labels and human oversight are distinct provenance claims; the selected datasets contain materially different combinations.

Buyer implication
Require a stage-level provenance manifest and test the label target relevant to the intended task.
Limitations
The reviewed methods are source-reported and version-specific. No universal advantage of human or synthetic labels is established.
Confidence
High for the documented provenance distinctions; unestablished for comparative training outcomes.
Reasoning
HelpSteer3 describes independent human preference annotations, UltraFeedback describes GPT-4 labels and FineWeb-Edu describes model-scored educational filtering. Calling these one annotation category would erase the origin of the supervision signal.
What would change this assessment
Independent task-matched validation with raw annotations and generation logs could support outcome comparisons or expose errors in the reported provenance.

Approved evidence: candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.independent-human-labels, next.claim.ultrafeedback.model_feedback, candidate.paperfull.fineweb.synthetic-educational-labels

Analytical judgment

agreement-needs-denominators

Released agreement and preference-pair totals cannot be interpreted without the independent-judgment and exclusion denominators.

Buyer implication
Request raw-to-retained counts, invalid-item rules, repeat labels, disagreement slices and corrected acceptance.
Limitations
The reviewed workflows differ in task and sampling. They cannot rank provider quality, and no common reliability measurement was executed.
Confidence
High for the methodological distinction; low for transferring a numerical agreement result between workflows.
Reasoning
HelpSteer3 selects agreeing labels and excludes disagreements; HelpSteer2 aggregates closest ratings; InstructGPT expands ranked sets into correlated pairs and usually uses one contractor per comparison. Final record totals therefore summarize different observation processes.
What would change this assessment
A common held-out task with independent raw judgments and the same exclusion rules could make reliability comparisons meaningful.

Approved evidence: candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.postfilter-consensus, next.claim.helpsteer2.qa, candidate.paperfull.instructgpt.human-ranking-sets, candidate.paperfull.instructgpt.single-contractor-comparisons

Analytical judgment

artifact-role-is-narrow

Named artifact attribution is strongest when it preserves the exact contribution stage and release rather than extending a brand association across a family.

Buyer implication
Ask for source-supported roles for the specific delivered artifact; keep recruitment, annotation, validation and authorship separate.
Limitations
These examples do not reveal contract values, contribution shares, exhaustive supplier lists or causal provider performance.
Confidence
High for the explicit scoped roles in this sample; incomplete for the broader supplier graph.
Reasoning
HelpSteer3 names Scale and Translated for different subsets; the Prolific case establishes recruitment through a researcher-owned interface; U-MATH credits Toloka AI and Gradarius with validation of professor-authored problems. These relationships support narrower claims than sole production.
What would change this assessment
Additional artifact-specific acknowledgments, contributor records or contracts could establish further stages or revise the scope.

Approved evidence: candidate.supplier.scale_ai.helpsteer3-contribution, next.claim.helpsteer3.translated, candidate.supplier.prolific.cohere-recruitment, candidate.supplier.toloka.umath-validation

Analytical judgment

benchmark-protocol-before-score

Benchmark family names alone are insufficient for comparing scores or deciding deployment readiness.

Buyer implication
Freeze task version, candidate responses, aggregation and execution environment, then inspect errors on the buyer’s actual task.
Limitations
No benchmark was executed for this report. The reviewed sources do not establish a universal deployment-quality ranking.
Confidence
High for protocol differences and stated limitations; unestablished for any new system’s performance.
Reasoning
RewardBench versions change scoring structure; TruthfulQA changes answer protocol and separates generation metrics; SWE-bench warns that passing tests does not ensure complete, efficient or readable solutions. The measures answer different questions.
What would change this assessment
Reproducible matched-protocol results and independently checked target-task outcomes could support a narrower comparative claim.

Approved evidence: next.claim.rewardbench.v1.scoring, next.claim.rewardbench.v2.scoring, next.claim.truthfulqa.metrics, next.claim.truthfulqa.binary_revision, candidate.paperfull.swebench.regression-test-scoring

Analytical judgment

commercial-denominators-stay-separate

The selected commercial disclosures cannot be combined into supplier market shares, production-capacity rankings or a common unit-cost comparison.

Buyer implication
Retain period, currency, organizational scope, active-window definition and acceptance basis; obtain a project-specific quote and availability check.
Limitations
Coverage is selected and incomplete. Missing disclosure is unknown, not zero; the observed figures are not matched measures.
Confidence
High for the incompatibility of these disclosed denominators; no confidence claim is made about market-wide shares.
Reasoning
Appen reports full-year consolidated and geographic-segment revenue, Scale reports cumulative contributor payouts with unspecified period and dollar currency, and Prolific distinguishes active participants from a waitlist without defining the active window. None supplies a matched current paid-work or human-data revenue denominator across suppliers.
What would change this assessment
Comparable segment accounts, audited activity windows and accepted-unit cost records across the same scope could permit limited financial or operational comparisons.

Approved evidence: candidate.supplier.appen.revenue-fy2025, candidate.supplier.appen.segments-fy2025, candidate.supplier.scale_ai.cumulative-payout, candidate.supplier.prolific.active-pool

2. Weekly developments

Method

This first-edition prelaunch baseline establishes a starting record rather than a weekly change series. Older findings first inspected now remain older findings. Source publication, event, capture, assertion and review dates have different meanings. There is no prior published edition in the report ledger against which to calculate changes, and the changed-claim list is deliberately empty.

Source-backed finding

Version changes already visible in the selected sources illustrate what a future weekly comparison must preserve. TruthfulQA creator documentation describes a January 2025 binary multiple-choice revision and incomplete revalidation of remaining questions and sources. RewardBench 2 uses a different response-comparison and aggregation protocol from RewardBench 1. These are artifact-specific changes, not a measured industry trend or a common performance time series.

Evidence: next.claim.truthfulqa.binary_revision, next.claim.truthfulqa.revalidation_gap, next.claim.rewardbench.v1.scoring, next.claim.rewardbench.v2.scoring

Source-backed finding

The selected supplier sources include Toloka’s January 2026 self-serve launch description and Mercor’s APEX-Agents 1.1 release account. Toloka describes client-calibrated quality rules and revision routing. Mercor reports 80 tasks per professional domain refined through three expert audits. These first-party accounts document the described offerings and release process; they do not independently demonstrate delivery quality or a change in supplier rank.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.toloka.self-serve, candidate.supplier.mercor.apex11-release

Method

The retained weekly source cutoff is Friday 6 November 2026 at 17:00 Pacific. New captures used in this preparation occurred after that cutoff, so this snapshot cannot be represented as an eligible on-time weekly edition. Later review can inspect an already captured version without changing its capture date. A future comparison should identify actual prior inputs, additions, corrections and withdrawals, rather than relabel late preparation as publication.

3. Market structure

Analysis

The sample spans overlapping capability categories. Appen describes expert alignment, agentic, multimodal, physical-AI and evaluation services; Scale describes tailored expert-curated generative-AI training datasets and model evaluation; Toloka describes demonstrations, preferences, evaluation and hybrid synthetic/human workflows. This overlap makes a single broad supplier category insufficient for procurement. Compare the requested artifact, domain and delivery responsibility within each offering, while treating capability pages as first-party descriptions.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.appen.offering, candidate.supplier.scale_ai.data-engine, candidate.supplier.scale_ai.evaluation, candidate.supplier.toloka.hybrid-offering

Analysis

Provider identity, product and business scope must remain separate. Scale describes Data Infrastructure and AI Applications as two primary business segments. Turing describes AI-lab data and RL-environment work alongside enterprise agent development, but these are described activities, not independently reported financial segments. Turing Frontier is specifically a US-based expert-access product. Neither that geography nor its verification description defines the whole Turing talent pool.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.scale_ai.segments, candidate.supplier.turing.business-separation, candidate.supplier.turing.frontier-product, candidate.supplier.turing.expert-pool

Analysis

Delivery model is another independent axis. Prolific distinguishes researcher-managed participant access from managed complete-dataset collection. Snorkel describes non-exclusive Data Series products refreshed quarterly; Mercor markets ready-to-license datasets as well as custom research partnerships. A buyer choosing between access, catalog licensing and commissioned production should assign responsibility for task design, rights, quality assurance and revisions explicitly. The disclosures do not supply matched prices or outcomes.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.prolific.platform-managed, candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.data-series, candidate.supplier.mercor.catalog, candidate.supplier.mercor.custom

Source-backed finding

Workforce figures use incompatible denominators. Mercor advertises more than five million domain experts, without an activity window or paid-assignment denominator. Turing advertises more than five million experts across more than 250 domains, without current active or paid counts. Appen’s FY2025 report describes a global crowd above one million. Prolific reports over 300,000 active participants and over one million waitlisted, but does not define the active window.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.mercor.expert-pool, candidate.supplier.turing.expert-pool, candidate.supplier.appen.crowd-network, candidate.supplier.prolific.active-pool

Analysis

These network disclosures cannot rank available production capacity. Toloka’s general annotator, AI tutor and domain-expert tiers describe workforce structure rather than headcount. Scale describes matching through background, skills, profiles and prior Outlier work. For a constrained project, ask how many qualified contributors can start during the requested period, how availability was checked and how many completed paid work on comparable tasks. Those project-specific denominators are not established here.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.toloka.workforce-tiering, candidate.supplier.scale_ai.matching, candidate.supplier.prolific.active-pool, candidate.supplier.turing.expert-pool

4. Technical landscape

Source-backed finding

The pinned InstructGPT paper describes human demonstrations and rankings as separate stages. For reward-model collection, labelers rank four to nine model responses per prompt; pairwise comparisons derived from one ranking are correlated. PPO input prompts do not carry per-prompt human labels because learned reward supplies that stage’s feedback. The prompt dataset primarily uses early Playground submissions, explicitly excluding production API customer data, with labeler-written prompts used to bootstrap collection.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.instructgpt.human-ranking-sets, candidate.paperfull.instructgpt.unlabelled-ppo-inputs, candidate.paperfull.instructgpt.playground-prompts

Analysis

DPO changes the optimization procedure without removing the need to inspect preferences. Under its KL-constrained objective and preference-model assumptions, it learns through a direct policy objective without a separately fitted reward model and RL loop. Its summarization experiment reuses existing human preferences with a different SFT model, while the controlled IMDb experiment uses classifier-generated preference labels. These are distinct provenance and transfer conditions, not evidence that data collection becomes unnecessary.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.dpo.direct-policy-objective, candidate.paperfull.dpo.reused-human-summary-preferences, candidate.paperfull.dpo.synthetic-imdb-preferences

Source-backed finding

The reviewed DPO empirical evaluation covers models up to six billion parameters. Larger-model scaling, broader distribution shift and reward over-optimization remain further-study questions in that source. Its summary-judgment validation recruits 25 volunteer raters, mainly a Stanford STEM convenience sample, with one late volunteer excluded from final analysis. This validates selected summary matchups under the study design, not universal superiority over PPO or a population-representative preference standard.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.dpo.tested-model-scale-limit, candidate.paperfull.dpo.volunteer-human-validation

Source-backed finding

The pinned FineWeb paper describes about 15 trillion GPT-2-tokenized tokens from 96 Common Crawl snapshots and uses individual per-crawl MinHash deduplication in its final pipeline. Controlled ablations use 1.71-billion-parameter models, equal token budgets commonly of 28 billion or 350 billion tokens, and selected academic benchmarks. The paper notes scale and unaligned benchmark-only limitations; its deduplication choice is not proof that global deduplication is universally inferior.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.fineweb.crawl-release-lineage, candidate.paperfull.fineweb.per-crawl-deduplication, candidate.paperfull.fineweb.ablation-scale

Analysis

FineWeb-Edu makes the label-target distinction particularly concrete. Llama-3-70B-Instruct scores 460,000 sampled pages for educational quality. A classifier uses 410,000 model-scored pages and holds out 50,000 against those synthetic scores. Validation against that target measures model-score agreement, not independent educator agreement. A buyer seeking educational usefulness should therefore test the intended learner population and content level separately from reproducing the filtering classifier.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.fineweb.synthetic-educational-labels, candidate.paperfull.fineweb.synthetic-classifier-groundtruth

Source-backed finding

HelpSteer3-Preference assigns each sample to three to five independent human annotators, requesting preference direction, strength or invalidity and brief reasons. Internet fact-checking is permitted; LLM tools are prohibited during annotation. Its documented coverage does not include intersections between General, STEM, Code and Multilingual areas, such as non-English code prompts, and is limited to 14 programming languages, 13 natural languages and the described text tasks.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.independent-human-labels, candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.missing-domain-intersections

Analysis

Human baselines also need their own provenance. MMLU reports 34.5% accuracy for unspecialized MTurk respondents, while its approximately 89.8% expert level is an estimate using examination percentiles and educated guesses, not a measured all-subject expert panel. TruthfulQA uses separate external researchers for reference-label validation on 100 questions and a human-answer baseline on 250. These populations and procedures cannot be combined into a representative human standard for expert-data procurement.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.mmlu.unspecialized-human-baseline, candidate.paperfull.mmlu.estimated-expert-baseline, candidate.paperfull.truthfulqa.external-validation-sample

Analysis

The selected papers support a technical comparison by mechanism: a direct preference objective, a synthetic quality filter and repeated human judgments answer different questions. None of these reviewed methods alone specifies the best workflow for a new buyer task. A useful pilot should hold the task, model, training budget and evaluation protocol constant while varying the proposed data intervention; otherwise an observed change cannot be assigned to annotation or optimization alone.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.dpo.direct-policy-objective, candidate.paperfull.fineweb.synthetic-classifier-groundtruth, candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.independent-human-labels

5. Provider dossiers

Method

These dossiers compare documented requirements and evidence types. Offering and process statements are primarily first-party disclosures, not independent operational audits. Named artifact roles are narrower than general capability. Absence of a reviewed disclosure means unknown in this sample. Each pilot should request the actual delivery scope, contributor requirements, acceptance procedure, rights package and responsible contracting entity rather than substitute a brand-level description.

Analysis

Appen describes coding deliverables including repository tasks with verified patches, debugging traces, preference pairs and test-generation data. It describes project agreement metrics, continuous gold questions and adjudication, with evaluation teams separate from training-data producers. For a coding-data pilot, request sample patches, reproducible test results and the boundary between those teams. The disclosures establish proposed controls and deliverable types; they do not independently establish their implementation or achieved accuracy.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.appen.coding, candidate.supplier.appen.adjudication, candidate.supplier.appen.evaluation-separation

Analysis

Mercor describes expert-written prompts, rubrics, golden solutions and long-horizon workplace environments, with expert vetting and peer review plus automated controls. Its APEX-Agents 1.1 account gives a named benchmark example, while its revised judge account acknowledges increased false negatives versus the naive grader. A professional-task pilot should therefore inspect rubric coverage and both error directions. These benchmark-specific disclosures cannot rank Mercor’s general delivery performance or establish customer training use.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.mercor.task-construction, candidate.supplier.mercor.peer-review, candidate.supplier.mercor.apex11-release, candidate.supplier.mercor.grader-tradeoff

Analysis

Prolific describes experience- or assessment-selected AI taskers across modalities and offers both participant access and managed collection. A researcher-authored Hosking/Cohere case identifies it as participant provider; researchers used their own modified Potato interface. That role establishes recruitment, not Prolific authorship or adjudication of labels. Buyers should decide whether they need a recruitable sample or a delivered artifact and specify who designs, hosts and accepts the annotation workflow.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.prolific.ai-taskers, candidate.supplier.prolific.modalities, candidate.supplier.prolific.platform-managed, candidate.supplier.prolific.cohere-recruitment

Analysis

Scale offers expert-curated training datasets and targeted red-teaming, and describes automated review with human standard-setting and edge-case review. NVIDIA’s pinned HelpSteer3 card attributes General, STEM and Code annotations to Scale; the paper separately names Scale’s sourcing and management role for those subsets. These narrow roles strengthen artifact attribution without establishing all-family production, ownership, contract value or causal model gains. A buyer should ask which stages the proposed engagement actually covers.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.scale_ai.data-engine, candidate.supplier.scale_ai.evaluation, candidate.supplier.scale_ai.quality, candidate.supplier.scale_ai.helpsteer3-contribution, candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.scale-subset-recruitment

Analysis

Snorkel describes non-exclusive, quarterly refreshed dataset and environment products and expert authoring, peer review and comparative evaluation. Its captured Finance Reasoning page describes 79 question-answer pairs co-created with financial experts, while its LLM-judge evaluation is a separate step. The page lacks an immutable release identifier and shown publication date. Buyers considering catalog reuse should request exact version bytes, refresh semantics and permission terms before treating later downloads as the same evaluated artifact.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.data-series, candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.expert-review, candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.finance-benchmark

Analysis

Surge offers SFT demonstrations, RLHF data, human evaluation, and agentic environments with behavior verifiers. OpenAI’s pinned GSM8K card says Surge helped expand collection after an initial Upwork-collected set; it describes re-solving by different workers and repairing or discarding disagreements. This is a historical, dataset-specific account from the card, not a full-paper review or proof of sole authorship. Ask for comparable validation records for the proposed new task.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.surge_ai.human-feedback, candidate.supplier.surge_ai.rl-environments, candidate.supplier.surge_ai.gsm8k-contribution, candidate.supplier.surge_ai.gsm8k-quality

Analysis

Toloka describes demonstrations, preference and evaluation data, domain-expert taxonomy design and human verification of generated data. The pinned U-MATH card credits Toloka AI and Gradarius math experts with validation of professor-authored curriculum problems. That is a validation role, not sole origination; performance-image tables were not inspected. Buyers should distinguish authoring, checking and adjudicating in the statement of work and request evidence that each role matches the required domain.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.toloka.hybrid-offering, candidate.supplier.toloka.taxonomy-quality, candidate.supplier.toloka.umath-validation

Analysis

Turing Frontier offers verified US-based scientific and professional experts, with claimed identity, background and work-history checks. An anonymous company case describes human-driven sandbox sessions across more than 150 tools and skills and over 120,000 preference pairs contrasting compliant actions and failure modes. These are case-specific company disclosures. Pair counts are not worker or task counts, and model-improvement language is not independently demonstrated here. Request representative trajectories, failure coverage and acceptance evidence.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.turing.frontier-product, candidate.supplier.turing.verification, candidate.supplier.turing.sandbox-capture, candidate.supplier.turing.preference-delivery

6. Dataset and benchmark landscape

Source-backed finding

HelpSteer2’s pinned card describes 0–4 human ratings for helpfulness, correctness, coherence, complexity and verbosity, complemented by preference labels and justifications. Prompts are mostly user-contributed ShareGPT material, with approximately 5% human-generated by Scale AI; responses come from ten early in-house LLMs. Scale’s attribution concerns attribute annotation. Human prompt contribution, model response generation and human scoring must remain separate provenance fields.

Evidence: next.claim.helpsteer2.attributes, next.claim.helpsteer2.source_mix, next.claim.helpsteer2.scale

Source-backed finding

The pinned HelpSteer3 collection includes Preference, Feedback, Edit, Edit-Quality and Principle configurations. Its 40,476 Preference samples and 95%/5% train/validation split describe that configuration, not the union of every configuration. Scale is attributed only to Preference General, STEM and Code annotation, and Translated only to Preference Multilingual. Neither attribution establishes Principle annotation, prompt translation, every release or a complete supplier list.

Evidence: next.claim.helpsteer3.configurations, next.claim.helpsteer3.preference, next.claim.helpsteer3.scale, next.claim.helpsteer3.translated, candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.translated-subset-recruitment

Source-backed finding

HH-RLHF separates chosen/rejected preference artifacts from red-team transcripts and their intended uses. Helpfulness contains base, rejection-sampled and online tranches, whereas harmlessness uses base-model data. The historical study recruited US master-qualified MTurk workers and Upwork contractors with writing spot-checks and lightweight vetting. It did not select workers by direct agreement metrics and retrospectively reports about 63% researcher-worker agreement. That study-specific figure is not platform-wide quality.

Evidence: next.claim.hh_rlhf.format, next.claim.hh_rlhf.purpose, next.claim.hh_rlhf.recruitment, next.claim.hh_rlhf.quality_limits

Source-backed finding

SHP uses existing human-written Reddit posts and comments with collectively inferred preferences, rather than separately elicited individual pairwise ratings. Its card table lists 385,563 pairs across 18 subreddits, split by post ID into 348,718 train, 18,436 validation and 18,409 test pairs. These are documented counts, not independently recounted rows. The inspected terms discuss Reddit scraping and user ownership without granting a standard permissive dataset license; current rights were not adjudicated.

Evidence: next.claim.shp.collective_preferences, next.claim.shp.split, next.claim.shp.license

Source-backed finding

OASST1’s full April 2023 corpus summary lists 161,443 messages, 35 languages, 461,292 quality ratings and more than 13,500 volunteers. Its ready-for-export subset is smaller: 88,838 messages in 10,364 trees, excluding spam and deleted messages, versus 66,497 trees in the all export. A synthetic-capable schema prevents an all-human-only inference. Guidance distinguishes writing, classification and ranking, but instructions do not establish universal contributor compliance.

Evidence: next.claim.oasst1.volunteer_corpus, next.claim.oasst1.exports, next.claim.oasst1.guidelines

Source-backed finding

UltraFeedback samples instructions from six named upstream sources and four models from a 17-model pool per instruction. GPT-4 supplies numerical and textual feedback on instruction-following, truthfulness, honesty and helpfulness. Creator documentation records a December 2023 overall-score correction using thresholds and re-annotation; this is README-level evidence because the named implementation path returned 404 at the pinned commit. No transitive supplier attribution follows from upstream source membership.

Evidence: next.claim.ultrafeedback.sources, next.claim.ultrafeedback.model_feedback, next.claim.ultrafeedback.correction

Analysis

RewardBench 1 scores whether a chosen response outranks a rejected alternative and uses section weighting, including math/code balance. RewardBench 2 averages six categories: five compare one chosen response with three rejected responses, while Ties uses a distinct correctness-and-margin metric. A score change across versions is therefore not a matched improvement measurement. The pinned RewardBench 1 card’s ODC-BY aggregation declaration also preserves component-license obligations, including listed noncommercial sources.

Evidence: next.claim.rewardbench.v1.scoring, next.claim.rewardbench.v2.scoring, next.claim.rewardbench.terms

Analysis

MMLU illustrates the separation between family, distribution and executable procedure. The pinned HF card describes 57 multiple-choice subjects and five development examples per subject. Separately inspected creator code requests five demonstrations, reduces them when context cropping requires, chooses the highest A–D token log probability and computes sample-weighted accuracy. No benchmark execution or byte-level association between those local CSV inputs and the pinned HF distribution was established in this review.

Evidence: next.claim.mmlu.tasks, next.claim.mmlu.evaluation

Analysis

TruthfulQA’s pinned HF distribution contains generation and multiple-choice configurations of the same 817 questions; the later creator repository describes revised binary A/B evaluation. Generation truthfulness and informativeness, MC1 accuracy, MC2 probability mass and new binary accuracy measure different behavior. HHH alignment is another distinct task, using binary response comparisons across helpfulness, honesty, harmlessness and other categories. Its co-author approval process belongs to benchmark creation, not independent review of this report.

Evidence: next.claim.truthfulqa.legacy_configs, next.claim.truthfulqa.binary_revision, next.claim.truthfulqa.metrics, next.claim.hhh_alignment.task, next.claim.hhh_alignment.authorship

Analysis

Original full SWE-bench contains 2,294 issue/PR-derived tasks from twelve Python repositories. Later Verified is described separately as 500 engineer-confirmed solvable problems with OpenAI Preparedness. Current pinned collection documentation describes scraping, patch/test requirements, environment configuration and execution validation; it does not prove that every documented step ran for every original instance. Keep the original task release, later subset and inspected repository workflow separate when reproducing a comparison.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.swebench.original-full-construction, candidate.paperfull.swebench.python-scope, next.claim.swebench.verified_scope, next.claim.swebench.collection

7. Human expertise and operations

Analysis

HelpSteer3’s three-to-five independent annotators supply more information than the final aggregate preserves. Postprocessing first removes samples with any invalid annotation, retains the three most agreeing annotations and excludes cases with remaining disagreement greater than two preference-strength points. The aggregate averages and rounds those retained labels; released ties are not used in reward-model training. Ask for raw and retained denominators before interpreting post-filter agreement as reliability across all attempted work.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.independent-human-labels, candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.postfilter-consensus

Analysis

HelpSteer2 similarly aggregates the three closest ratings and describes subsequent vendor and creator QA, with disagreement annotations separately identified. InstructGPT’s most comparisons are labeled by a single contractor for cost reasons, while ranked sets generate correlated pairs. Repetition, filtering and pair expansion affect different denominators. A pilot should report independent judgments per item, exclusions, corrected acceptance and unresolved disagreements rather than present one final agreement statistic as a complete quality measure.

Evidence: next.claim.helpsteer2.qa, candidate.paperfull.instructgpt.single-contractor-comparisons, candidate.paperfull.instructgpt.human-ranking-sets

Analysis

Recruitment evidence should retain its stage. The InstructGPT paper identifies Scale and Upwork as channels for roughly 40 contractors in total across demonstrations, comparisons and main evaluations, without assigning shares. Upwork is not thereby established as the annotation employer or managed producer. The HelpSteer3 paper names Scale and Translated for sourcing and managing specified subsets. Those relationships do not transfer ownership of prompts, responses or the whole dataset family to the recruiter.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.instructgpt.scale-recruitment-channel, candidate.paperfull.instructgpt.upwork-recruitment-channel, candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.scale-subset-recruitment, candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.translated-subset-recruitment

Analysis

The selected provider descriptions offer different quality controls: Appen describes gold questions and adjudication; Snorkel describes calibration, dual-expert review, consensus, sampling and programmatic checks; Scale describes automated review with human experts setting standards and handling edge cases. These are useful implementation questions, not comparable outcome measurements. Ask which decisions are automated, which require domain review, what escapes each stage and whether the customer can inspect disagreements and rejection appeals.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.appen.adjudication, candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.quality-controls, candidate.supplier.scale_ai.quality

Analysis

Human contribution is broader than recruited annotation. SWE-bench’s authors say collection, evaluation and experiments did not use crowdsourcing or recruited task workers, yet they manually created executable contexts and relied on human repository contributions. TruthfulQA’s authors wrote the questions and performed the main generation evaluations under model-name and prompt blinding. These examples show why no external supplier and no human labor are different conclusions; source provenance must retain author and upstream developer work.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.swebench.no-recruited-task-workers, candidate.paperfull.swebench.manual-execution-contexts, candidate.paperfull.truthfulqa.authored-questions, candidate.paperfull.truthfulqa.blinded-human-evaluation

Method

Before a pilot, define an accepted unit: verified solution, adjudicated comparison, usable trajectory or licensed record. Specify expertise checks, task instructions, independent judgments, permitted tools, invalid-item handling, escalation and rework. Measure first-pass acceptance separately from corrected acceptance. Sample rejected work and difficult cases as well as accepted deliveries. This is a proposed acceptance procedure, not a claim that any reviewed provider currently meets it.

8. Commercial evidence

Source-backed finding

Appen’s FY2025 audited financial statements report consolidated customer-contract revenue of USD 230.774 million for 1 January–31 December 2025. Appen Global and Appen China report USD 127.874 million and USD 102.900 million respectively. These geographic operating segments do not isolate expert generative-AI or human-data revenue. The figures are reported full-year group and segment revenue, not annualized pace, transaction volume or a matched measure of this report’s supplier category.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.appen.revenue-fy2025, candidate.supplier.appen.segments-fy2025

Source-backed finding

Scale’s FY2025 statement, approved in June 2026, reports nearly $1 billion paid cumulatively to hundreds of thousands of contributors across more than 150 countries. The phrase is to date without a specified start or end. The captured statement does not establish a dollar currency beyond its symbol, and no payment reconciliation was inspected. This is neither company revenue nor annual wages nor a current active-workforce measure.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.scale_ai.cumulative-payout

Source-backed finding

Prolific’s captured FAQ lists usual platform fees of 42.8% for corporate and 33.3% for academic or nonprofit customers, but the bound passage does not explicitly define the percentage denominator; managed services are custom-priced. Its minimum permitted participant rates are GBP 6 or USD 8 per hour, with GBP 9 or USD 12 recommended. These are tariff statements and platform rules, not realized specialist earnings, margins or net take rates.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.prolific.fees, candidate.supplier.prolific.minimum-rewards

Analysis

Snorkel’s public expert statement describes project-based pay, weekly processing of accepted contributions through HireArt and opt-in matching. That does not establish typical earnings or guaranteed assignments. Alongside Prolific’s minimum-rate rules, it shows why pay basis, acceptance condition and available work must be asked separately. A buyer’s total accepted-unit cost should include design, recruiting, tooling, rework and internal review; no matched full-cost comparison is supplied here.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.payment-and-choice, candidate.supplier.prolific.minimum-rewards, candidate.supplier.prolific.platform-managed

Research gap

The approved sample does not establish comparable revenue for the relevant human-data activities across suppliers, matched gross margins, standardized project prices or independently reconciled accepted-unit costs. Missing disclosure is unknown, not zero. No market-size estimate or supplier revenue ranking is derived. Future commercial comparisons need the same currency, period, organizational scope, gross/net basis and service definition before arithmetic can support a conclusion.

9. Governance

Analysis

Security disclosures require scope checks. Scale states SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO/IEC 27001:2022; Appen describes SOC 2 Type II, a HIPAA-specific solution and named facility options; Snorkel states SOC 2 Type 2 and engagement-start control scoping. Underlying reports, certificate coverage and customer deployments were not inspected. Prolific describes ISO 27001 and Cyber Essentials while treating SOC 2 Type 2 as a future plan. These statements cannot be flattened into equivalent verified controls.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.scale_ai.security-disclosure, candidate.supplier.appen.security, candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.security-scope, candidate.supplier.prolific.security

Source-backed finding

Toloka’s published guidelines use different personal-data conditions by task category. For third-party personal information they list both anonymization before upload and consent agreements. Public-space images have their own blurring rule, exception and consent condition; collection from Tolokers requires lawful collection, a named administering entity, purpose and linked privacy policy. These are platform requirements, not proof of dataset compliance. Linked additional collection guidelines were not separately captured and remain unknown.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.toloka.pii-rules

Analysis

A privacy notice must cover the service being assessed. Mercor’s captured website notice excludes work.mercor.com, so it cannot establish expert-platform consent, work-product rights or retention. Turing’s June 2025 policy lists AI development and training among personal-information uses, while Surge’s December 2021 standard terms grant a perpetual internal-business and service-improvement license for labeling User Data. Neither establishes every negotiated deliverable’s ownership or project-specific contributor consent; inspect the applicable contract chain.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.mercor.privacy-scope, candidate.supplier.turing.personal-data-ai-use, candidate.supplier.surge_ai.user-data-license

Analysis

Workforce and subcontractor paths deserve the same specificity. Scale describes access through third-party BPOs or other providers and Outlier. Snorkel’s policy contemplates staffing partners and client disclosure; Appen’s privacy statement describes contractor access controls and confidentiality. These disclosures identify possible processing structures without enumerating every actual project subcontractor. Request the real processing chain, access locations, retention rules and flow-down obligations for the engagement instead of assuming the contracting brand performs every stage directly.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.scale_ai.subcontractors, candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.workforce-partners, candidate.supplier.appen.privacy-subcontractors

Analysis

Worker protections also have limited scope. Scale describes advance notice, refusal options and wellness resources for sensitive-content safety work; Toloka requires advance disclosure and acknowledgement for sensitive content and describes human review of automated restrictions. Prolific forbids under-18 recruitment and ordinarily directly identifying data collection, subject to exceptions. These are disclosed practices or rules, not audited compliance. A pilot should verify the consent flow, escalation route and practical ability to decline the actual task.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.scale_ai.sensitive-content, candidate.supplier.toloka.sensitive-content, candidate.supplier.toloka.automated-appeal, candidate.supplier.prolific.participation-rules

Analysis

Documentation and incident disclosure supply evidence without eliminating residual risk. Mercor disclosed impact from compromised LiteLLM versions in March 2026 in a June investigation account; impact and remediation were not independently audited here. FineWeb’s authors acknowledge significant remaining potentially toxic or harmful documents. Datasheets for Datasets explicitly says documentation alone is not complete mitigation. Request verifiable remediation, sampled content checks and an update process rather than interpret a policy or datasheet as a guarantee.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.mercor.incident, candidate.paperfull.fineweb.harmful-content-remains, candidate.paperfull.datasheets.documentation-mitigation-limit

10. Buyer decision guides

Analysis

For expert preference data, compare HelpSteer-style repeated judgments with the proposed provider workflow, not with raw pair totals. Require the intended domain, language, independent-label count, reason format and invalid-item policy. HelpSteer3’s missing domain intersections make a useful acceptance question: does a non-English coding requirement actually occur in the proposed sample? Pre-register difficult slices and inspect performance before exclusions, as well as the final retained set.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.independent-human-labels, candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.missing-domain-intersections, candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.postfilter-consensus

Analysis

For software-agent evaluation, original SWE-bench provides an issue/PR and test-based reference design, with solved patches required to pass both FAIL TO PASS and PASS TO PASS tests. The paper warns passing tests does not guarantee completeness, efficiency or readability. The inspected harness documentation separately records likely infrastructure failures. A pilot should report environment failures separately, reproduce tests and manually inspect a sample of passing patches under the buyer’s own repository and language scope.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.swebench.regression-test-scoring, candidate.paperfull.swebench.python-scope, next.claim.swebench.evaluation

Analysis

For professional reasoning tasks, Mercor describes workplace environments and golden solutions; Snorkel’s finance example separates expert question creation from LLM judging; Toloka’s U-MATH example separates professor authorship from expert validation. Compare these roles against the requirement: realistic authoring, domain validation or scalable scoring. Ask for task provenance, rubric failure cases and judge calibration. None of these examples establishes a supplier’s superior finance, mathematics or professional competence.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.mercor.task-construction, candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.finance-benchmark, candidate.supplier.toloka.umath-validation

Analysis

For reward-model or truthfulness selection, freeze the benchmark protocol before comparing outputs. RewardBench versions alter candidate sets and aggregation. TruthfulQA separates generation truthfulness and informativeness from multiple-choice measures, and its authored questions may over- or underestimate deployment truthfulness. Require a matched version, scoring implementation, held-out target tasks and error review; do not convert a benchmark win into a general claim about safe or truthful deployment.

Evidence: next.claim.rewardbench.v1.scoring, next.claim.rewardbench.v2.scoring, next.claim.truthfulqa.metrics, candidate.paperfull.truthfulqa.deployment-generalization-limit

Analysis

For catalog licensing, a refreshed product and an upstream aggregate create different checks. Snorkel describes quarterly refreshed non-exclusive products; the pinned RewardBench 1 card requires compliance with component licenses; SHP’s inspected card does not grant a standard permissive license. Ask for exact artifact identity, intended commercial use, upstream restrictions, redistribution rights and what changes under a refresh. A public download or catalog label cannot by itself settle the buyer’s reuse rights.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.data-series, next.claim.rewardbench.terms, next.claim.shp.license

Method

A proposed pilot acceptance sheet should state the deliverable and denominator; qualifying domain and language slices; blind held-out evaluation; allowed tools; annotation and adjudication rules; error severity; first-pass and corrected acceptance; turnaround; rights and security scope; and cost per accepted unit. Set thresholds before inspecting results. Record failures and exclusions, retain source versions and reserve a customer-reviewed sample for deciding whether the pilot supports expansion.

11. Research outlook

Analysis

One testable outlook is that mixed human/model pipelines will require more granular provenance. FineWeb-Edu uses synthetic educational scores; UltraFeedback uses GPT-4 feedback; Toloka markets human verification of generated data. These examples show several integration patterns in this sample, not their market prevalence. The assessment would strengthen with task-level logs distinguishing generation, selection, correction and independent validation, and weaken if those distinctions fail to predict acceptance on matched buyer tasks.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.fineweb.synthetic-educational-labels, next.claim.ultrafeedback.model_feedback, candidate.supplier.toloka.taxonomy-quality

Analysis

A second hypothesis concerns executable tasks and scoring reliability. Surge offers agent environments and behavior verifiers; Turing describes captured sandbox sessions; SWE-bench documents regression tests and infrastructure categories. This suggests a useful research agenda around environment reproducibility, verifier coverage and failure attribution. It does not establish a market shift or causal training gains. Repeated executions on matched frozen tasks, with independently checked outcomes, would be more informative than catalog growth alone.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.surge_ai.rl-environments, candidate.supplier.turing.sandbox-capture, candidate.paperfull.swebench.regression-test-scoring, next.claim.swebench.evaluation

Analysis

A third question is how release-specific documentation changes practical reuse. Datasheets recommends accompanying updated versions of infrequently changing datasets with updated documentation and identifies dynamic datasets as an implementation challenge; TruthfulQA’s revision and RewardBench’s protocol change show why version identity matters. Evidence that a revised release reproduces prior results under a matched protocol would strengthen comparability. Missing bytes, changed scoring or unresolved correction histories should instead narrow conclusions to the inspected version.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.datasheets.updated-version-docs, next.claim.truthfulqa.binary_revision, next.claim.rewardbench.v2.scoring

Research gap

Priority expansion remains the agreed inventory, not a smaller denominator selected for convenience. More suppliers, full-source papers, dataset families and benchmark families need dispositions before comprehensive synthesis is justified. Missing domains, languages, access conditions, current work availability and comparable commercial evidence should be recorded explicitly. Future outlook statements must distinguish observed sample changes, proposed mechanisms and forecasts; this baseline supplies no market-growth forecast or universal performance prediction.

12. Methods and appendices

Method

The approved graph is the factual boundary for this draft. Stable assertions bind subject, nontransitive predicate, typed value or object, source version, locator, excerpt digest, qualifications and actual review references. Every factual or analytical report paragraph cites exact approved claim IDs. Methods and research gaps are explicitly labeled. Historical imports remain in the underlying graph; this synthesis does not promote their inherited descriptions into newly reviewed facts.

Method

Assertion approval records distinct author, source-verifier and adversarial source-content invocations. It concerns support for exact wording, entities, quantities and scope. Separate report evidence-auditor and adversarial invocations must review the frozen synthesis and bind its digest together with the approved graph digest before import. AI review is labeled Separate AI review. It is not human peer review, independent experimental replication, security certification or a completed research-accuracy audit.

Method

Coverage is calculated from qualifying graph entities and approved assertions, not inferred from paragraph length or raw assertion count. Distinct paper works, dataset families and benchmark families remain separate from versions, subsets, mirrors, code workflows and study artifacts. A full-source review describes the inspected documentation scope, not proof that every release or operational claim is complete. Candidate, quarantined, rejected, duplicate and historical-only records cannot inflate qualifying launch coverage.

Research gap

All launch coverage floors remain unmet: eight of 39 legacy dispositions, eight of 60 qualifying suppliers, eight of 150 reviewed paper works, eight of 60 dataset families and five of 20 benchmark families. No eligible core denominator has been frozen, so the required 90% disposition is unestablished rather than a measured screening recall. No inventory is narrowed to make these numbers pass; unresolved cases and preserved source packets remain available for further review.

Method

Launch also requires two separate real audits. A source-anchored holdout of at least 200 assertions must achieve at least 98% precision and 95% recall with no critical false attribution. A distinct 200-record eligibility screening sample must recover at least 190 records and at least 90% of each major stratum. Freeze membership before adjudication, preserve source-bound row decisions and independent receipts, and recompute metrics from rows. Test fixtures and generated accuracy summaries do not count.

Research gap

Neither completed audit is supplied for this graph. The baseline therefore reports no achieved precision, recall, screening recovery or critical-attribution result. Source capture after the retained Friday cutoff is another publication blocker. The report remains prelaunch with archive status not_published, empty editions and no DOI. Prepared data, website visibility, archive publication and mirror synchronization are separate states; none substitutes for the missing scientific and publication gates.

Analysis

Datasheets for Datasets proposes reflective human documentation, asks about collection participants and compensation, and describes a development process refined over roughly two years. These are useful disclosure prompts, not evidence that every later datasheet follows them or that compensation is fair. The paper also notes documentation overhead and limits. This report uses those questions to expose unknowns while requiring source evidence for answers, rather than automatically converting a filled template into assurance.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.datasheets.nonautomated-reflection, candidate.paperfull.datasheets.worker-compensation-disclosure, candidate.paperfull.datasheets.development-process, candidate.paperfull.datasheets.documentation-mitigation-limit

Method

Corrections should identify the affected assertion, exact source version and locator, proposed wording and reason. Preserve original captures and actual review dates; later inspection cannot backdate a source. Reproduction should bind this report’s review digest and the graph’s canonical hash, publish only the permitted public projection and concise evidence, and exclude raw caches, credentials and private personal data. License statements remain descriptions of inspected terms rather than blanket legal determinations.
